leftover: WORDS I HAD TO SPLIT under rule 2, each one my decision: 'command' (having the right to be obeyed / issuing an order); 'Monday' (the day / the order it issues)
'must', 'obligated', 'can', 'optional': written as plain descriptions, their force lost
'we must abolish Mondays': an ought. Nothing in the chain ever arrives at it
'unemployed time': a figure of speech, written as the writer uses it

1.text: [GIVEN as undeniable] ALWAYS: a beginning is arbitrary

2.text: [GIVEN] Monday is the beginning of the week

3.text: ALWAYS: what is arbitrary lacks authority

5.text: Monday lacks authority SINCE it is a beginning

6.text: ALWAYS: what lacks authority, we have no duty to obey (my reading of 'cannot command our obedience')

7.text: [GIVEN] Monday issues a command: wake up

8.text: [CLAIMED] we have no duty to obey Monday

9.text: no duty to obey SINCE Monday lacks authority

10.text: ALWAYS: a command that goes unheeded is a suggestion

11.text: Monday's command is a command (a thing apart from the day itself)

13.text: Monday is a suggestion SINCE we have no duty to obey it

15.text: [CLAIMED] if enough people ignore Monday, it ceases to exist

16.text: it ceases to exist if ignored SINCE it is optional

18.text: Monday being gone MAKES Tuesday become Monday

19.text: if something becomes Monday, then there is a Monday

20.text: [CLAIMED] the week collapses into a single day

21.text: the week is one day SINCE Tuesday becomes Monday

23.text: time is unemployed SINCE the week is one day (and one day cannot be a week)

25.text: ALWAYS: leisure is the basis of culture

26.text: [CLAIMED] sleeping in on Mondays saves civilization

27.text: we save civilization SINCE leisure is the basis of culture
